gen-fs-new-title-bitter: Tall, tightly linked letters give New Title a bold, modern bite, like a fine chain pulled across the line. Bitter's slab-serif body, with its huge lowercase and see-through s, keeps paragraphs grounded.
gen-dafont-woodgod-manrope: Woodgod's lowercase climbs almost to the capitals, giving it a vintage, commanding stance with wide channels into every bowl. And Manrope handles the quiet work, its bright curves and single-width line staying clean and approachable in a sans.
gen-dafont-alien-encounters-general-sans: General Sans reads smoothly, its steady pen pressure and tall x-height filling each line with no snag at any bend. And Alien Encounters supplies the otherworldly gaps between letter pairs, so the sans can simply carry on.
gen-dafont-azonix-archivo: Azonix lets its capitals sit barely above the lowercase, so words take a moment to knit together, though they stay crisp when small. And Archivo, a plain sans, opens its curves outward, so a long page of it stays approachable.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-asap: Big round bowls in the lowercase give Bloody its commanding, slightly menacing look. Asap's open-arc c forms and body height nearly matching its capitals make the sans-serif feel readable and straightforward.
gen-dafont-capture-smallz-satoshi: Capture Smallz stamps out big-bodied lowercase letters with a raw, tactical bluntness that grabs attention at once. Satoshi, a plain sans, simply stays readable, with its soaring x-height and unsqueezed e.
gen-dafont-dogica-switzer: Wide, heavy and blunt, Dogica stretches its lowercase up toward the capitals with generous tracking. Switzer, a sans-serif with wire-like strokes and a tall waist line, is the one that stays friendly over the long run.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-work-sans: Work Sans is a modern sans with high mean lines and c tips that never creep toward touching. Early GameBoy brings playful, stretched-out swagger with a soft weight gradient, while Work Sans just keeps the text moving.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-archivo: Archivo's curves open outward instead of curling in, and its commanding x-height gives the sans-serif real presence under Bushcraft. Paragraphs would move along easily, with nothing closed off.
gen-dafont-college-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads loose and curvy, a wire-like monoline plain sans with tall lowercase and stubby ascender tips. College hits hardest with thick curves and big counters, while Epilogue is the one made to be read.
